paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations. Row 1 (Baseline): Significant massive activations and attention sinks emerge after the 6th layer. Row 2 (SDPA Gating): Reduced activations and no attention sinks observed. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating): Similar activations to Row 2 but with residual attention sinks. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid): Massive activations and attention sinks resemble the baseline.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The chart illustrates the maximum activation values across layers for four different output types in a baseline model configuration, highlighting the emergence of “massive activations” and “attention sinks” after the 6th layer. The x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 22, with labeled ticks at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 22). The y-axis represents the “Max Activation Value,” scaled linearly from 0 to 1600, with labeled ticks at intervals of 200 (0, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600). Four distinct lines are plotted, each corresponding to a different output type as indicated by the legend: “attn_output” (blue dashed line with circular markers), “attn_residual” (orange dotted line with circular markers), “ffn_output” (green dashed line with triangular markers), and “ffn_residual” (red solid line with circular markers).

The “attn_output” line (blue dashed) remains near zero until approximately layer 20, after which it rises sharply to a value of approximately 200. The “attn_residual” line (orange dotted) starts near zero, rises sharply to a peak of approximately 1500 at layer 5, remains elevated until layer 15, then drops to approximately 1000 before falling to near zero after layer 20. The “ffn_output” line (green dashed) begins near zero, rises to a peak of approximately 1000 at layer 5, then drops sharply to near zero by layer 7, with a minor secondary peak near layer 14 at approximately 900 before falling to near zero again. The “ffn_residual” line (red solid) remains near zero until layer 5, then rises sharply to a peak of approximately 1600 at layer 5, remains elevated until layer 15, then drops to approximately 1400 before falling to approximately 600 at layer 20 and rising slightly to approximately 600 at layer 22.
model_annotations.Chinese: This line chart, titled "Massive Activation of baseline," displays the maximum activation values across layers for four distinct components of a transformer model: attn_output (blue dashed line), attn_residual (orange dotted line), ffn_output (green dashed line), and ffn_residual (red solid line). The x-axis, labeled "Layer," ranges from 0 to 22 with linearly spaced integer tick marks, indicating the layer index. The y-axis, labeled "Max Activation Value," ranges from 0 to 1600 with linearly spaced tick marks at intervals of 200, representing the peak activation magnitude. The chart illustrates that all four lines remain near zero until approximately layer 5, after which they exhibit sharp increases. The red solid line (ffn_residual) rises most steeply, reaching a peak value of approximately 1580 at layer 5, then stabilizes at a high level above 1400 until layer 20 before dropping sharply to around 600. The orange dotted line (attn_residual) follows a similar pattern, peaking near 1580 at layer 5 and remaining above 1400 until layer 20. The green dashed line (ffn_output) shows a more erratic pattern, rising to a peak of approximately 1200 at layer 5, then dropping sharply to near zero by layer 7, with a brief spike to approximately 1100 at layer 15, and then falling again. The blue dashed line (attn_output) remains near zero until layer 20, after which it rises to a value of approximately 200.
model_annotations.English: This line plot, titled "Massive Activation of baseline," illustrates the maximum activation values across different layers for four components of a transformer model: attn_output (blue dashed line), attn_residual (orange dotted line), ffn_output (green dashed line), and ffn_residual (red solid line). The x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 22 with tick marks approximately every 5 units. The y-axis represents the "Max Activation Value," scaled linearly from 0 to 1600. The plot shows that for all four lines, activation values remain near zero up to layer 5. After layer 5, all lines exhibit a sharp rise, reaching peak values between layers 6 and 10, with the ffn_residual (red) and attn_residual (orange) lines reaching approximately 1550 and 1500, respectively. The ffn_output (green) line also rises sharply, peaking around 1100 at layer 6 before dropping to near zero by layer 10. The attn_output (blue) line remains near zero until layer 20, then rises to approximately 250. The ffn_residual (red) line remains high from layer 6 to layer 20, then declines sharply after layer 20, dropping to approximately 550 at layer 22. The attn_residual (orange) line follows a similar trend to the ffn_residual, peaking around 1550 and declining to approximately 550 at layer 22. The ffn_output (green) line remains low until layer 10, then rises to approximately 1000 at layer 15 before declining again. The attn_output (blue) line remains low until layer 20, then rises to approximately 250.

The blue dashed line, labeled 'attn_output', starts near zero, remains low until layer 6, then rises sharply to approximately 200 at layer 22. The orange dotted line, labeled 'attn_residual', begins near zero, spikes sharply to approximately 1500 at layer 6, remains high until layer 15, then declines to approximately 1400 at layer 22. The green dashed line, labeled 'ffn_output', starts near zero, rises sharply to approximately 1300 at layer 6, drops sharply to near zero by layer 10, rises again to approximately 1200 at layer 14, then falls to near zero by layer 22.
